content.text:
V2CoO6 (mp-19311) alone accounts for the observed pattern.

- **Strong peaks:** the simulated V2CoO6 pattern reproduces every strong observed peak, at both the right positions and the right relative intensities. Observed peaks at 18.9°, 20.8°, 26.2°, 27.0°, 29.3° and 31.65° (two-theta) have intensities of about 22, 53, 100, 44, 81 and 93. The simulation gives about 20, 52, 100, 44, 82 and 94 at the same places.
- **Weaker peaks:** the simulation also produces the 36.5–38° cluster and the weak feature near 13.2°.
- **Other candidates:** I also simulated Eu(BO2)3 (mp-22248) and CeTi2O6 (mp-1105722). Both fit worse. Eu(BO2)3 predicts its strongest peak near 17.4°, where the observed pattern is flat. CeTi2O6 puts strong peaks at 26.5° and 28.2°, which don't line up with the observed ones. I did not simulate the other six candidates.
- **Second phase:** no observed peak is left unexplained, so I'm not adding one.

{"present": ["mp-19311"], "confidence": 0.93, "note": "Every strong observed peak (18.9, 20.8, 26.2, 27.0, 29.3, 31.65 deg) matches the simulated V2CoO6 pattern in position and relative intensity, with no unexplained peaks left over."}
